newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds climb with Treasuries late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds climb with Treasuries late.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities caught a favorable breeze late on Wednesday and sailed modestly higher, keeping pace with Treasuries.
Buying by hedge funds and foreign central banks propped Treasuries up in the afternoon, Treasury market analysts said. Mortgages took their cue from that late uptick, mortgage traders said.
In late trading, pass-throughs were up 6/32 to 8/32 in current and discount coupons and were unchanged to up 5/32 in premium coupons.

Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.0 percent paper climbed 7/32 to 99-06/32, yielding 103 basis points over 10-year Treasuries. Fannie Mae 7.5 percent coupons were up 6/32 to 100-30/32, and Freddie Mac 7.0s were 7/32 higher at 99-07/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 7/32 at 6.13 percent.
Earlier, the Commerce Department announced the trade deficit grew 10.1 percent in September, to $11.34 billion.
In a Reuters poll after the data, 24 economists on average said third-quarter gross domestic product grew at a 1.8 percent rate, compared with Commerce's previous estimate of 2.2 percent.
